The program is called Shot Spotter and is nothing new. They've been around in CA and NY since the early 90's. They just keep rolling out more nationwide.

Shot Spotter works via an array of microphones that matches sound prints on file when it detects a sound louder than a certain threshold. It has nothing to do with "echolocation."

You know the layout of your house, right? Let's say your ears are the array. You hear a window break. Because you have a "sound print" (memory) of what it sounds like glass breaking, you know it's probably a window. You also know the layout of your house and based on how far away it is, you know (based on where things are located) where the breakage came from.

If the burglar wrapped a hammer in a rug and smashed the window, it would sound different yes, but you have enough memory to know what it is still.

Shot Spotter records are insane. They have peaks logged for every caliber you can think of, in every configuration, various types of fireworks and car noises (to prevent false positives), etc. Whoever told you it works by echo location lied to you.
